reports.execution: Native SOAtest REST execution using the installed add-on and bundled Java 21 runtime.
reports.hosting: MCP creates the scenario; REST authors Groovy Extension Tools because neither authoring API exposes standalone custom tools. Each host obtains the installed JUnit Executor descriptor, calls its native configuration initializer, sets the class folder/class/method, and invokes native CustomTool.apply using the real hosting MethodToolContext as the error-output context. The installed add-on and native wrapper generate the errors recorded by SOAtest.
cases: JUnit 4 passing assertion control.
JUnit 4 assertion mismatch.
JUnit 4 IllegalStateException with an IllegalArgumentException cause.
JUnit 4 expected exception that passes.
All four JUnit 4 methods: two native diagnostics combined into one failed host test.
All three JUnit 3 methods: an assertion failure and runtime error combined into one failed host test.
An absent method produces a fatal native CustomToolException.
An absent class produces a fatal native CustomToolException with the ClassNotFoundException cause.
reports.limitation: These are Extension Tool hosts invoking the real native custom-tool wrapper, rather than persisted standalone JUnit Executor test steps. Report XML is unchanged. Both regular JUnit errors and fatal add-on configuration errors were emitted as FuncViol.

reports.authoring: MCP creates the scenario. The SOAtest desktop Add Test wizard creates an actual JUnit Executor step; its class folder and NativeJUnitCases class are configured in the native editor and saved by SOAtest.
reports.execution: Native SOAtest REST execution of the saved standalone JUnit Executor, using bundled Java 21.
cases: One standalone executor runs the four JUnit 4 methods: passing assertion, failing assertion, nested runtime failure and passing expected exception. The two native diagnostics belong to one failed SOAtest test.
reports.note: This confirms the native report type independently of Extension Tool hosting.

preservation: Each XML file is an unchanged native report.xml, obtained from a REST execution archive or native CLI report directory. Tests run offline without SOAVirt or ParaBank.
coverageLimit: Native fixtures demonstrate SOAtest's FuncViol, VisualDifference and ChangeImpact. The installed JUnit Executor was exercised as a saved standalone tool and through its native custom-tool wrapper: assertion, runtime and configuration errors emitted FuncViol. The shared schema also includes ExecViol (a base type without a known SOAtest producer), UnitViol (used by unit-testing products) and RuntimeViol (still produced by C/C++test, but no longer by SOAtest). Controlled SOAtest fixtures cover the three native kinds and an explicitly synthetic unknown kind; specialized unit/runtime formatting is outside this transformation's scope.

marketplaceInvestigation.scope: Current extension entries and their nested documentation, including JUnit/TestNG Executor, Burp Suite, Java Virtualization Agent, Event Monitor File Logger and transport/listener tools.
